clue.text: Officer's hair alarms criminal

indicators.note: a criminal arrangement is a wrong one, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: An officer's appalling haircut sends everyone into a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Officer stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: air marshal is one senior officer rank in the RAF.

clue.text: Fifth of puzzles by Serpent? Run!

indicators.note: a fifth of a word here means its fifth letter, counted from the front

explanation.surface: A puzzle-lover spots a serpent and bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: Run looks like a command to flee, but it is the noun: a ladder is a run in tights or stockings. 'By' just places the snake next to L, and snakes-and-ladders is the hidden joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A British sense: a ladder is the line of broken stitches Americans call a run in tights.

clue.text: Digits rung by husband to get wife, perhaps

definitions.text: Digits rung by husband to get wife, perhaps

parts.note: reads as fingers and a wedding ring or bells, but digits are numerals and rung means dialled on the phone

parts.words: by husband to get wife, perhaps
parts.note: suggests winning a bride; it is only a husband calling home

explanation.surface: A husband does something with his fingers to win a wife, as if proposing.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word points to marriage and rings; the plain reading is a string of numbers a husband dials to reach his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description in disguise: a telephone number is the digits you ring to reach someone.

clue.text: Having rejected help, family gets bitter criticism

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read back to front

parts.note: aid = help, turned round to DIA
a tribe is a family group or clan

explanation.surface: A proud family turns down help and gets a tongue-lashing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Having rejected help reads as the family's pride; it is the instruction to reverse AID, and 'gets' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a diatribe is a sustained, bitter attack in words.

clue.text: Minicab company over in Bavaria

explanation.surface: A minicab firm has taken over in southern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Bavaria is a German state, so 'over' is to be put into German. A minicab is a British term for a private hire car booked by phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Uber is a company whose app books private cars, and über is the German word for over.

clue.text: Kit found in poor European army unit

indicators.note: something found in a place is inside it, so the first item goes inside what follows

parts.note: a rig is a kit or outfit; it goes after the first letter of BAD

explanation.surface: Kit is discovered in a shabby European army unit.
explanation.walkthrough: Kit sounds like army gear, which fits the military surface, so it is easy to read it as part of the definition rather than a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brigade is a large army formation made of several battalions.

clue.text: Penniless man getting rid of Liberal for Republican

indicators.note: getting rid of something throws it out
one thing for another means in exchange

parts.note: R = Republican, put in where the L was

explanation.surface: A man ruins himself by switching parties from Liberal to Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloke is everyday British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: broke is the informal word for having no money at all.

clue.text: At home with pal or close to being out?

explanation.surface: Staying in with a friend or nearly away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Out here means in flower, as blossoms come out. The question mark flags that sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom by way of a pun: a plant in bud is close to flowering, that is, to coming out.

clue.text: We supply cards doddery elders will receive 1st of April

definitions.note: the definition speaks as the dealers themselves

indicators.note: doddery means shaky on one's feet, so the letters wobble into a new order
to receive something is to take it in, so the A joins the elders' letters
the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A greeting-card firm says its elderly customers will get cards on April Fool's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests greeting cards posted to old folk; the answer deals playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A description in the first person: dealers are the players who hand out the cards.

clue.text: Horror writer beginning to make lyrical work

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, writer of horror tales

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A horror writer is starting to try his hand at poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Beginning to make reads as 'starting to create'; it only supplies the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: a poem is a work of verse, and lyrical here just means poetic.

clue.text: Confidential informant releasing red-hot tape

indicators.note: releasing the letters sets them free to settle in a new order

explanation.surface: A whistleblower leaks an explosive recording.
explanation.walkthrough: Releasing tape fits a leak story so well that it hardly reads as an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A name turned byword: Deep Throat was the secret Watergate source, and now means any anonymous insider.

clue.text: Her tract upset one of four joint rulers

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A pamphlet she wrote offended one of the co-rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset reads as offended; it is the signal to rearrange HER TRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: From the Greek for four-ruler: a tetrarch governed one quarter of a divided realm.

clue.text: Romeo possibly sleeping around is natural

indicators.note: one thing around another encloses it

parts.note: Romeo is the code word for R, the 'possibly' allowing it as one example

explanation.surface: Romeo sleeping with all and sundry is only natural.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo tempts you to think of the lover; here it is the letter R from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A less common sense: inbred can mean innate or deep-rooted, as in an inbred sense of fairness.

clue.text: Fart once and be worried for 'friend'

indicators.note: worried means shaken up and fretful, so the letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters; 'and' just joins the pieces

explanation.surface: Break wind once and fret about what your friend will think.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'friend' flag the looser sense of a supporter or patron.
explanation.definitionFit: A looser sense: a friend of a charity or museum is a patron who gives money.

clue.text: Some might say Tory inclination shows good sense

definitions.meaning: read as being minded towards the political right

indicators.note: hedges the claim, warning that one meaning is a playful reading of the word

explanation.surface: A claim that leaning Conservative is simply common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tories are Britain's Conservative party, on the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: right-mindedness is sound judgment, and split playfully it is a mind set on the right.

clue.text: Act the same as one on X-Factor covered by China

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so I comes first
a thing covered by another has it all round

parts.note: china = mate, from rhyming slang china plate
it = that indefinable appeal, the X factor; it sits after the first letter of MATE

explanation.surface: A contestant on The X Factor, backed by China, copies another act.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make X-Factor look like the TV talent show; really it is the quality called 'it'. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to imitate is to act the same way as someone else.

clue.text: Have doubts about teacher tied up in hearing

indicators.note: what is in someone's hearing is what they hear, so go by the sound

parts.note: Miss = a teacher, trussed = tied up

explanation.surface: Doubts about a teacher bound up in a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearing looks like a legal hearing; it is the sound signal. British pupils call a female teacher Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to mistrust someone is to doubt them.

clue.text: Good books stuffed in drawers by well-meaning folk?

definitions.note: the second definition describes the things rather than naming them: books that are stuffed in drawers
definitions.meaning: the Good Book is a set name for scripture

definitions.text: stuffed in drawers by well-meaning folk?
definitions.meaning: sounds like hoarding; it is the Gideons placing copies in hotel bedside drawers

explanation.surface: Kindly people cram improving reading into chests of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gideons, a Christian group, place copies of scripture in hotel bedside drawers.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by custom: the Good Book is the usual nickname for scripture found in hotel drawers.

clue.text: Told, if on diet, to go running

indicators.note: letters sent running scatter and come back in a new order

explanation.surface: A dieter is instructed to take up jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: Told looks like the start of a sentence of advice; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to be notified is to be formally told.

clue.text: One bowled over by PM's address on good bit of news

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: the Prime Minister lives at Number Ten Downing Street

indicators.note: a bit of a word is here its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is bowled over by good news in the Prime Minister's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Address looks like a speech, but it is where the PM lives. Bowled over means knocked down literally, as a pin in bowling is.
explanation.definitionFit: A literal reading of an idiom: a tenpin is a skittle knocked over by the ball.

clue.text: Old flame I'll, after picking up, send to Coventry?

indicators.note: picking up a signal, as a microphone does, means we go by what is heard

parts.note: ex = old flame, followed by I'll

explanation.surface: A jilted lover vows to banish a former partner once they get back in touch.
explanation.walkthrough: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom for refusing to speak to them; the question mark allows exile as a stronger form.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: banishing someone is a harsher form of sending them to Coventry.

clue.text: Chap who got up to go to work in the field?

definitions.text: Chap who got up to go to work in the field?

parts.note: sounds like waking early; the setter means he mounted a horse

parts.words: to go to work in the field?
parts.note: sounds like farm labour; the field is the field of battle

explanation.surface: A farmhand rises early to go and work in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: Got up suggests waking and the field suggests farming; here he climbs into the saddle and rides into battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A description in disguise: a mounted soldier gets up on his horse to fight in the field.

clue.text: A meeting with minister for old dictator

explanation.surface: A summit with a government minister lined up for a former despot.
explanation.walkthrough: Meeting with just sets A beside MIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Idi Amin ruled Uganda by terror in the 1970s.

clue.text: At front, cadet helping injured para gets shot, of course

indicators.note: the front of each word is its first letter

parts.note: first letters of Cadet Helping Injured Para

explanation.surface: A cadet helping a wounded paratrooper is shot, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Of course reads as 'naturally'; it means on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf term: a chip is a short lofted shot onto the green.

clue.text: South American magazine back issues

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end to the start

parts.note: Time, the US news magazine, placed after S

explanation.surface: Back numbers of a South American magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: South American looks like one unit; it splits into South and American magazine, and back issues is a red herring for the verb issues.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to emit is to issue or send out, and issues is a verb here.

clue.text: Typical example of no-good swine in English book

indicators.note: no good means without G, the abbreviation for good
one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a tome is a big book, following E, with PI in between

explanation.surface: A worthless pig in an English book is a typical example of something.
explanation.walkthrough: No-good reads as worthless, but it tells you to remove G from PIG.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an epitome is a perfect embodiment of a type.
